tested_scope: One bounded official-GitHub documentation audit of deleted immutable-release tag-name reservation across repository immutability disable/reenable, repository rename/transfer, reservation-specific status/rejection observability, and GitHub Free/no-finite-monthly-quota acceptance.

public_sources.title: Immutable releases - GitHub Docs
observations: A published immutable release locks its associated Git tag while the release exists.
If the immutable release is deleted, the tag can then be deleted but the same tag name cannot be reused.

GitHub documents protection against repository resurrection: deleting a repository and creating a new repository with the same name does not allow reuse of tags associated with immutable releases in the original repository.

public_sources.title: Immutable releases are now generally available - GitHub Changelog
observations: Disabling release immutability does not affect releases created while it was enabled; those releases remain immutable.
Existing releases are not made immutable merely by later enabling the repository setting.

public_sources.title: REST API endpoints for repositories - immutable releases
observations: GitHub documents repository-level check, enable, and disable endpoints for immutable releases.
The check endpoint reports whether repository immutability is enabled and whether it is owner-enforced; it is not documented as a historical deleted-release tag-reservation status endpoint.
Enable/disable operations document generic 204 success and 409 conflict statuses, not a reservation-specific create-ref/tag rejection contract.

public_sources.title: Preventing changes to your releases - GitHub Docs
observations: Repository or organization settings can enforce immutable releases for future releases.

observations.disable_reenable_lifecycle: Documented compositional support is stronger than Part112: disabling immutability does not alter already-created immutable releases, and GitHub separately states that deletion of an immutable release leaves its tag name non-reusable. This supports the sequence disable -> delete immutable release -> tag-name reservation remains, with later re-enable irrelevant to that already-immutable release. The documentation does not expose a historical reservation object to inspect.
observations.rename_transfer_lifecycle: The bounded official-source retrieval did not surface an explicit guarantee that deleted immutable-release tag-name reservation identity survives repository rename or ownership transfer. Repository delete/recreate same-name resurrection protection is documented, but rename/transfer is a distinct transition and is not generalized here.
observations.reservation_observability: A repository-level immutable-releases status endpoint exists, but no reservation-specific GET/status endpoint or stable reservation-specific Git/REST rejection contract was surfaced in this bounded audit.
observations.free_no_monthly_quota_gate: The bounded official-source retrieval did not surface explicit GitHub Free availability or an explicit no-finite-monthly/trial/paid-quota statement for immutable releases. Acceptance therefore fails closed on the Phase-1 quota/plan gate.

inferences: The disable/reenable child is narrowed: existing immutable-release status persists through disabling according to GitHub's changelog, so disabling is not itself evidence that historical tag-name reservation can be cleared.
Repository resurrection protection cannot be safely generalized to rename or transfer without explicit source evidence or a permitted direct probe.
A feature-status endpoint is not equivalent to a durable reservation witness; current enablement state and historical reserved-name state are separate proof objects.

phase1_acceptance.reason: At least three hard obligations remain unproven in this bounded leaf: rename/transfer continuity, reservation-specific observability/rejection semantics, and GitHub Free/no-finite-monthly-quota availability.

scope_guard: Only current multi_agent role-local continuation and the bounded official GitHub sources listed above were used. No O, other-role, downstream, legacy, shared-ledger, scheduler or protected-primary semantic input/effect was used.
